text:
carla: FYI the q8-canary we rolled earlier today is showing a coherent metric delta on the eval harness, holding canary until we triage.
ben: saw that - which metric?
eva: looks like ExactMatch_downstream and our reranker score distribution shifted on the same commits as the quant kernel bump.
carla: exact. quick snippets from harness logs: ```
[eval-runner] model=redwood-7b-q8 commit=ab12f3
metric=exact_match baseline=0.742 canary=0.713 delta=-0.029
metric=rerank_auc baseline=0.912 canary=0.871 delta=-0.041
```
frank: those deltas are big enough to block GA. any chance this is a reporting mismatch vs real outputs?
carla: I thought that initially. I ran the same prompt set locally against the canary binary and the outputs look reasonable, but the harness scoring pipeline gives different tokenization lengths for some examples.
ben: tokenization difference how? did the tokenizer model change?
eva: we shipped the tokenizer patch in #3784 earlier today (normalization tweak). Could be orthography leading to lower EM.
frank: also the quant pipeline changed the KV eviction heuristic. If prefix caching behaves differently we might produce different completions under same seeds.
carla: tried rerunning with the old tokenizer + new runtime, and with new tokenizer + old runtime. Results: 
- old tok + new runtime: delta -0.004 (almost baseline)
- new tok + old runtime: delta -0.026 (close to canary)
So looks like tokenizer patch is the major signal.
ben: nice bisect. so root cause likely the tokenizer normalization. How did that get into the eval commit graph?
eva: the tokenizer change was merged into the model assets repo yesterday to fix token alignment for multilingual tests. CI didn't flag because unit token counts stayed within tolerance.
ci-bot: deployment-notice: rolled canary to staging at 2026-03-20T09:12:34Z by deployer-bot
frank: two action items: 1) hold the canary rollout 2) revert tokenizer change in model assets or add a compatibility shim in the harness scorer.
carla: I'm creating a revert PR for the tokenizer normalization now: #3899. Also opening a small scorer shim PR that normalizes inputs the old way for the eval harness only (to avoid blocking other teams).
eva: for release decision: prefer revert in assets, then re-run full eval CI. If revert is risky, scorer shim + extra canary run is acceptable.
ben: agree. also add a quick metric-level assertion in CI: if EM delta < -0.01 AND tokenization mismatch rate > 0.5% fail early.
ci-bot: CI status: eval-harness/canary-run queued -> running (stage: scoring)
carla: re-run queued, tagging @product and @eng-runtime so they're aware.
frank: postmortem note: we need a gated acceptance test for tokenizer changes that compares eval harness scores on a fixed seed set before landing. I'll draft a proposal.
eva: +1. Also let's add a telemetry check that verifies that scorer accepts tokenizer version metadata and emits it to the dashboard so we can correlate.
ben: +1 on metadata. For now I'm pausing the dedicated canary auto-roll to prod until we get a successful re-run. :no_entry_sign:
carla: update: revert PR #3899 opened and CI started. I'll paste link in thread once green.
ci-bot: PR 3899 build: success -> merged by carla at 2026-03-20T10:01:10Z
carla: merged revert. kicking off full eval CI run now.
ci-bot: eval-harness/full-suite started (run id=20260320-877)
frank: thanks everyone. once the full-suite finishes we'll decide to resume rollout. If metrics return to baseline we'll resume; if not, we continue rollback and escalate.
eva: adding a postmortem checklist item to require scoring compatibility checks for any tokenizer or decode-path change.
ben: small follow-up: can someone open a dashboard card that shows tokenizer-version tag per run? helps incident triage later.
carla: will do. closing hold for now but keeping canary frozen until run finishes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
